systematic_causes.cause: Registry frame legitimately extends past the outermost printed tick (or starts before the first) to fit the actual plotted data/frame margin -- the project's own documented canonical benign pattern (design doc 7.44, using paper 10939 fig 3(a) as the worked example).
systematic_causes.note: Within this, three same-paper clusters share one literal root cause (one axis-frame decision reused across every panel, not independent per-panel coincidences): paper 18668 (12 entries, x always 300-850K vs printed 300-800K), paper 27759 (5 entries, x always [350 or 300]-1000K vs printed 400-1000K), paper 3733 (6 entries, x always 450-900K vs printed 500-900K). A related sub-cause recurs across many singleton entries: when a registry endpoint is exactly 0 (a natural physical floor for e.g. resistivity/concentration/thermal conductivity, common in this domain) while the first printed tick is a nonzero round number, the audit script's ratio check is structurally unable to verify agreement there (division by/of zero), so it always reports 'disagreement' even though the pattern is the ordinary benign one -- this affects 17037, 18869, 34286, 44283/38965 within this group.

systematic_causes.cause: Unit-space difference: registry.json and ground_truth.json are internally self-consistent in Starrydata's raw SI units for this entry, but the printed axis is in the paper's own display unit (or Kelvin-vs-Celsius offset) -- these are simply backlog from the 2026-09-02 'store in display units' migration (commit 31bd7e9 / design 7.47) that has not yet reached every entry. Not an error; will resolve once these entries get the same display-unit conversion already applied to most of the dataset.
systematic_causes.note: Confirmed transforms: 446 (x3, Kelvin<->Celsius, offset -273.15), 21682 (x2, V/K -> uV/K, x1e6), 4173 (V/K -> uV/K, x1e6), 5902 (V/K -> uV/K, x1e6), 4965 (V/K -> uV/degC, x1e6), 34286 (W/m/K^2 -> uW/cm/K^2, x1e4), 44283/38965 (ohm*m -> mOhm*cm, x1e5). 29352 also fits this family (W/m/K^2 -> uW/K^2cm, x1e4) but an independent affine+GT-containment cross-check flagged it as not perfectly clean, so it is carried at medium rather than high confidence.

systematic_causes.cause: Genuinely suspect ground truth: one entry (18759/12217) has an evidence-text-acknowledged outlier curve (one of 4 digitized curves sits ~2 orders of magnitude below the other three, explicitly left 'not yet independently reconciled against the chart' by whoever verified the entry) which plausibly explains why the range doesn't cleanly fit a single SI<->display conversion factor.
systematic_causes.note: Not newly discovered here -- the entry's own evidence text already flags this as open.

Registry is stored in Kelvin (273.15-723.15K); the printed axis is in degC. Implied transform: display = SI - 273.15 (pure Kelvin<->Celsius offset). The naive multiplicative check (k_min=0 because label_min=0) is meaningless here by construction (division involving 0); the *additive* offset is exact at the low end (0 - 273.15 = -273.15) in every one of this paper's 3 panels, confirming the transform. The high end differs by degrees Celsius per panel (400 for 4a's own printed axis, 500 for 4b/4c) even though all 3 panels share literally the same registry range -- ordinary per-panel margin on top of the same offset, not a new problem (evidence text for 4a: 'matches the chart panel (a)'s 0-450 degC axis').
